finding: Three different standards sit behind the word advisor: an adviser fiduciary duty (care and loyalty), the broker-dealer Regulation Best Interest standard, and the CFP Board fiduciary commitment; which applies depends on the registration and credential of the specific professional and is stated on that firm's Form CRS.
conditions: US readers; investment advice about securities and financial planning. State rules, insurance agents, banks and trust companies are outside the sources read.
whatWouldChange: A change to Regulation Best Interest or the SEC adviser interpretation, or CFP Board code revisions.

takeawayPlan: A fiduciary must act in your best interest; an SEC-registered investment adviser owes that as a duty of care and loyalty, a broker owes the separate Regulation Best Interest standard, and a CFP professional commits to it by code. Applies to anyone paying for investment advice; conflicts of interest remain, so read the firm relationship summary and ask. Evidence basis: reported (SEC, CFP Board, Investor.gov). Changes if the person is registered only as a broker or holds neither registration. Next step: search the person on Investor.gov and ask in writing which standard applies.
